title: The supplied projection mate on a shifted structure sheaf
statement: Use the derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], their canonical K-flat tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback] and direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For a morphism f, an adjunction p:Lf^*\dashv Rf_* with counit \epsilon and a natural isomorphism t:Lf^*(-\otimes^L-)\simeq Lf^*(-)\otimes^L Lf^*(-), write \pi_{p,t}(M,L) for the adjunction transpose of t_{M,Rf_*L} followed by 1_{Lf^*M}\otimes\epsilon_L. Let f:X\to Y be any morphism of schemes, with arbitrary derived localizations in a common morphism universe w, and p,t as above. Let L\in D(\mathcal O_X), M\in D(\mathcal O_Y), k\in\mathbf Z and an isomorphism M\simeq\mathcal O_Y[k]. Then \pi_{p,t}(M,L) is invertible. No quasi-coherence, compactness or separatedness is assumed.

proof.text: Identify the degree-zero structure sheaf with the monoidal unit using DerivedCategory.singleFunctorObjUnitIso. Use the explicit shifted tensor-unit homotopy complex, which is K-flat because the tensor unit is K-flat and K-flatness is stable under shifts. The single/quotient localization comparisons, the homotopy quotient unit isomorphism, and the localization shift comparison identify its image with the shifted structure sheaf. DerivedCategory.commShiftTensorRightQhObj and Functor.CommShift.ofIso then identify tensoring a shifted unit with translation. Translation by opposite integers gives both tensor-inverse isomorphisms. The associator and left unitor assemble tensorLeft of the shifted unit and tensorLeft of its opposite shift into an equivalence. This is the private proved helper shifted_unit_tensorLeft_isEquivalence, valid in the independent morphism universe w.

Use nonempty_derivedPullback_structureSheaf_iso to identify pullback of the degree-zero structure sheaf with the structure sheaf. Extract the shift-commuting structure from the specification of exists_derivedPullback; its commShiftIso transports this identification to every integer shift. Compose with the pullback image of the supplied isomorphism M to O_Y[k]. Functor.isEquivalence_of_iso transports the tensorLeft equivalences of the preceding step to tensorLeft M and tensorLeft (Lf* M).

For equivalences A and B and an isomorphism alpha:A followed by F to F followed by B, rotate alpha across the inverse-equivalence adjunctions a and b using mateEquiv.symm. Its formula consists of invertible units, alpha and invertible counits, so this rotated transformation beta is invertible. Apply conjugateEquiv_iso to beta and the composite adjunctions a.comp p and p.comp b. Expand the component formula: cancel the B inverse triangle, move the A inverse counit through p.unit by naturality, move the A inverse unit through alpha by naturality, and cancel the A inverse triangle. The resulting component is exactly p.homEquiv(alpha at G(L) followed by B.map of the supplied counit). This is the private proved helper equivalence_projection_mate_isIso; it does not assert invertibility for arbitrary mates.

Restrict the supplied bifunctor isomorphism t to the fixed first factor M. Its naturality at (id_M,a) gives the required natural isomorphism between tensorLeft M followed by pullback and pullback followed by tensorLeft of its image. Apply the preceding helper to the two tensorLeft equivalences. Unfold their component maps and id_tensorHom to obtain exactly the displayed supplied projection mate. All constructions include degree zero and empty schemes.

proof_origin.note: The existing unit-and-shift argument is implemented with explicit shifted K-flat units and a proved categorical rotation/conjugation calculation. Reuses the existing local derived-pullback structure-sheaf theorem instead of the monoidal-model dependency.
